name: Wu Chinese (Shanghainese) — Wugniu
notes: Wugniu (吴语学堂拼音, 'Wu Chinese School pinyin'), the IPA-adherent community romanization for Wu Chinese developed around 2016 by the Wu Chinese School, refining the earlier Wu Chinese Society pinyin (~2005). This spec models the Shanghainese (Urban Shanghai) variety of Wugniu, the same dialect `wuu.json`'s Han-script stub already names as its expected romanized input, exactly as `nan-Latn-poj` fills the equivalent gap for `nan`. INITIALS: Wu is distinctive among the Sinitic romanizations already in this dataset for keeping a genuine three-way laryngeal contrast at every place of articulation — voiceless unaspirated ⟨p t k ts c⟩, voiceless aspirated ⟨ph th kh tsh ch⟩, and TRUE VOICED ⟨b d g z j⟩ (not merely a spelling convention the way pinyin's ⟨b d g⟩ stand for unaspirated voiceless stops) — because Wu is the one Sinitic branch that never lost the Middle Chinese voiced obstruent series (`wuu.json`'s own notes on the parent `ltc` ancestor edge). ⟨gh⟩ /ɦ/ (voiced glottal fricative) is Wu's voiced counterpart to plain ⟨h⟩ /h/, completing the pattern rather than being redundant with it. The alveolo-palatal series ⟨c ch j sh zh⟩ /tɕ tɕʰ dʑ ɕ ʑ/ is written with its own dedicated letters (not derived from the alveolar series by a following-vowel rule, unlike POJ/PFS/BUC) because Wugniu's own source table gives them as phonemically distinct rows with their own sample characters, not an allophonic split of ⟨ts⟩/⟨s⟩. Checked (glottalized/tense) sonorant onsets that Wu's register system distinguishes from their plain counterparts (documented in the source's IPA column with a preceding ˀ, e.g. /ˀm/ vs /m/, /ˀn/ vs /n/) are not separately keyed here: Wugniu spells both members of several such pairs with the same letter, differentiated only by which of Wu's two tonal registers (yin/yang) the syllable carries, so the distinction is tonal/registral rather than segmental-orthographic and belongs with the tone-marking gap below, not as an invented segmental grapheme. VOWELS: the oral/nasalized vowel pairs (⟨a⟩/⟨an⟩ [ã], ⟨ua⟩/⟨uan⟩ [uã] …) are cited as separate final units per the source's own final-inventory table, since Shanghainese nasalization here marks a whole rime category rather than compose from a vowel plus a nasal consonant letter; front-rounded and central vowels (⟨oe⟩ [ø], ⟨eu⟩ [ɤ], ⟨y⟩ [ɿ] apical vowel, ⟨yu⟩ [ʮ] apical rounded vowel) are cited exactly to the source's Shanghainese-IPA column. CODAS: the nasal-coda finals ⟨-on⟩ /oŋ/ are given directly from the source table's velar-nasal-coda row; the full coda inventory beyond the small set of finals reconciled here is not yet exhaustively covered (RESEARCH tier, not PRODUCTION) — extending final coverage to the remainder of the source's finals table is future work, flagged rather than papered over. TONE — SCHEMA LIMITATION, same honest treatment as the other three Sinitic romanizations in this dataset: Wugniu marks tone with a trailing ASCII digit (1-5 in the Shanghainese scheme cited), which — like Jyutping's digit — is a free-standing character in its own tokenizer slot, not a diacritic fused into a vowel grapheme; this spec therefore does not add digit-suffixed grapheme keys (the same Cartesian-product violation flagged on `yue-Latn-jyutping`). `tone_inventory` records the digit-to-contour correspondence as metadata only. Wu's PROSODIC-WORD-SPANNING tone sandhi (`wuu.json`'s own notes: 'tone sandhi spanning whole prosodic words') is markedly more extensive than the syllable-local sandhi flagged on the other three Sinitic specs and is equally out of scope for the same missing-engine-capability reason (AGENTS.md §1): a `sandhi_rules`-like mechanism keyed on tone category across a whole prosodic word, not individual segments, would be needed, and enumerating around it is not an option.
